description.narrative:
In 2022 Oxfam Boliva contracted consultants to realize a first case study. Potential interested organizations also participated in trainings realized by Profundo and one member particiapted in the FFI General Assembly in June 22.
With the face to facetraining inSeptember and a visit by FFI, the work plan and budget for the coalition were further developed. 2023 will be a start up year with the focus on the realization of a number of activities as described in the work plan.
The coalition is made up of: OXFAM in Bolivia. It leads the coalition of institutions that will implement the FFI-funded project. It has specific activities to develop, mainly related to the coordination and implementation of events and spaces for reflection at national and international level. It is in charge of monitoring and ensuring the good and efficient execution of the resources within the framework of the strategy's objectives. Centre for Labour and Agrarian Development Studies, CEDLA. Local partner institution, linked to research on social, labour and environmental issues. Conducted the study on economic and productive activities and their sources of investment for OXFAM with FFI funding. CEDLA, as a partner, will be the institution in charge of contracting the otherentities of the coalition (FOBOMADE, FUNDESNAP, SDSN) for specific research. Foundation for the Development of the National System of Protected Areas, FUNDESNAP. Manages the trust fund that benefits protected areas in Bolivia. It has extensive experience in financial issues and is a member of REDLAC. It is part ofthe coalition and will be involved in research processes via CEDLA, through contracting as a consultant. Bolivian Forum on Environment and Development, FOBOMADE. Civil society institution working on socio-environmental issues. Experienced in monitoring Chinese investments and those of multilateral entities. It is part of the coalition and will be involved in research processes via CEDLA, through contracting as a consultant. Sustainable Development Solutions Network - Bolivia, SDSN. It is linked to the Bolivian Catholic University. It has worked on financial issues and their relation to climate change. It is part of the coalition and will be involved in research processes via CEDLA, through aconsultancy contract. Further development ofthe FFI activities related to the influencing of financial institutions and regulators do assume that further continuation in 2024 will be possible.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam has been working in Bolivia since 1988, through different local partners, including civil society organizations, associations, networks and different levels of the Bolivian Government, based on complementarity and mutual respect.
Our work in Bolivia focuses on reducing vulnerability through the sustainable exploitation of natural resources, political activism and increased productivity. We advocate for the creation of a more just society through our research and mobilisation of civil society andwe carry out long-term development projects that aim to reduce risk and increase resilience.
Priority social and geographical sectors
We strengthen the influencing capacities of indigenous populations, agricultural workers, and youth to promote public, redistributive, efficient, and transparent policies. We work with women and mixed-sex youth groups aiming to reduce violence, to empower them and promote better economic opportunities. We support land management, access to natural resources, risk reduction and adaptation of indigenous and rural communities. In Lowlands we provide support so that indigenous populations, communities, and farmers can overcome their vulnerability, exclusion, and the discrimination they face. We work with women, youth,and on indigenous population participation, adaptation,land management, and risk reduction in the main cities of Bolivia (La Paz, El Alto, Cochabamba, and Santa Cruz) as well as with thecities with rapid population growth located in the Amazons (Trinidad and Riberalta)..
